subject: nvabarPage() ... knowing what tab is active

messages.author: 57a95aa350db9768
messages.subject: nvabarPage() ... knowing what tab is active
parts:
Hi all. Maybe I'm missing something obvious, but is there a way to identify which navbarPage() menu item is active. In tabsetPanel() we can set the id argument to some value (say, "app_tabs") and then read that value on the server side. How is this same functionality replicated for navbarPage()?

Thank you.

messages.author: 8e965e659c833ed8
messages.subject: Re: nvabarPage() ... knowing what tab is active
parts:
Dan,

navbarPage also has an id parameter and it works the same way as tabsetPanel. Note that if you want to update the active page from the server this works too but currently only on a branch (this should be merged to master soon). To install the branch you can do:

devtools::install_github("shiny", "rstudio", ref = "feature/navbar-input-binding")

J.J.

messages.subject: Re: nvabarPage() ... knowing what tab is active
parts:
There's no branch documentation per-se, however once a branch is ready to be incorporated into master it typically becomes a pull request, which does typically have some additional documentation. Here are the currently outstanding pull requests (you can see the branch if any highlighted for each pull request):

https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/pulls

Showcase mode allows you to easily view an application and it's code at the same time (arranged either above/below or side-by-side) for purposes of illustration and learning. Here's what it looks like:

http://gallery.shinyapps.io/06_tabsets/?showcase=1

If you arrange the app and code side-by-side you'll also notice that reactive evaluation is automatically highlighted in the source view as you interact with the application.
